evidence.reason: `freezeStateRoot` is documented as copying the live state root into `<scratch>/a` and `<scratch>/b`, but it only writes captured files and never removes pre-existing destination files when a live file is absent. Because `mkdirSync(..., { recursive: true })` accepts existing directories, a stale `scratch/a/runner-disabled` (or any `SHADOW_FILES` entry) survives even when the live root lacks it, and `a` and `b` can start from different inputs. That contradicts the copy/snapshot intent and can corrupt the shadow comparison.
